Typst and MathTypst

Source: R/typst.R
typst.Rd

Text and formulas typeset by the Typst compiler and imported as vectorized mobjects. Typst() takes general Typst markup; MathTypst() wraps its input in display math ($ ... $). The typst command line compiler must be installed (see typst_to_svg_file()).

Usage

Typst(
  typst_code,
  font_size = DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
  typst_preamble = "",
  color = NULL,
  stroke_width = NULL,
  font_paths = NULL,
  track_baselines = FALSE,
  should_center = TRUE,
  height = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  ...
)

MathTypst(math_expression, typst_preamble = "", font_paths = NULL, ...)

Arguments

typst_code

Typst markup placed verbatim into the document body.

font_size

Font size (48 by default), applied by scaling after import.

typst_preamble

Extra Typst code inserted before the body.

color

Color for the parts Typst draws in black (white by default).

stroke_width

Stroke width override; NULL keeps Typst's strokes.

font_paths

Optional extra font directories for the compiler.

track_baselines

Keep per element baseline frames.

should_center

Center the result at the origin.

height, width

Optional target size; height overrides font_size.

...

Passed to SVGMobject() (style overrides such as opacity).

math_expression

Typst math without the $ delimiters; may contain {{ ... }} groups.

Value

A mobject: an R6 object of the class named by the function called. The objects whose names end in Class are the R6 class generators that these functions call.

Details

Typst renders in black; black parts take color while explicitly colored parts keep their color. Stroked parts drawn by Typst (fraction bars, underlines) keep a stroke width proportional to their size when stroke_width is NULL.

Parts can be selected with $select(key), which returns a VGroup() of the submobjects (not copies). Labels come from ordinary Typst labels (#box[body] <label>) or, in MathTypst(), from the {{ ... }} shorthand: {{ content : label }} names a group and {{ content }} is numbered automatically, so $select(1) is the first unnamed group (internally labeled _grp-0). Groups may be nested. Unlike upstream Manim, numeric keys are 1 based.

With track_baselines = TRUE, $baseline_frames lists the current (orig, right, up) points of each imported element's reference frame and $get_baseline_frame(submobject) returns one of them; both follow later affine transformations. As in upstream Manim, the reference frame is the SVG page frame (origin at the top left corner, one Typst point per unit).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs the typst compiler.
Typst("*Hello* from _Typst!_", font_size = 72)
eq <- MathTypst("{{ a^2 + b^2 : lhs }} = {{ c^2 }}")
eq$select("lhs")$set_color(BLUE)
eq$select(1)$set_color(YELLOW)
} # }
